runs.recorded: reconstructed from the sealed run record

events.title: Access token verified
events.detail: An authenticated read returned IQM Garnet's live architecture: 20 qubits. The saved token works.
events.explain: Every run starts by proving the key still opens the door — a read that costs nothing. If this fails, nothing else is attempted.

events.title: Four frozen CHSH circuits submitted
events.detail: Job ID 01a16625-2a81-7196-80fe-c16728f38b99 · 4 circuits × 1,024 shots · IQM Garnet.
events.explain: The circuits were frozen on 2026-10-20, before any account existed — a Bell test whose ideal answer is known exactly (S = 2.828). The machine cannot be graded against a prediction invented after the fact.

events.title: Counts returned from the real machine
events.detail: All 4,096 shots returned. Three settings agree (E ≈ +0.67); the fourth disagrees (E = −0.650) — the fingerprint of entanglement.
events.explain: Classical physics caps this pattern at S = 2.0. The sign flip in the fourth setting is exactly what quantum entanglement predicts and no local classical story can reproduce.

events.title: Analyzer grade: HIT
events.detail: CHSH S = 2.6640625, inside the locked HIT band [2.3, 2.90].
events.explain: The frozen analyzer — not a human — grades the counts against bands locked before the run. S = 2.664 is a real machine answering a quantum question, with honest noise below the ideal 2.828.

events.title: Credit ledger closed
events.detail: Cost: 1.00 credit for 2 seconds of QPU time. Balance 30.00 → 29.00, verified on the IQM dashboard.
events.explain: Every run reports before / spent / after. Proof should be cheap, and the price is part of the result.

events.title: Case opened: AEGIS-G1 Parallel Entropy Lanes
events.detail: Question, novelty check, circuit, analyzer and grading bands were locked on 2026-10-22, before this run.
events.explain: A real test starts before the machine: the question and the pass/fail bands are written down first, so the result cannot be graded with moving goalposts.

events.title: Pre-flight credit gate
events.detail: Balance before: 29.00 credits. Written estimate 2-6 credits, hard cap 6.0. Gate requires balance >= 12 after T0 — satisfied.
events.explain: The credit law: no run starts unless its worst case fits with margin. A run must never die mid-flight for lack of credits.

events.title: Credential verified against IQM
events.detail: Authenticated architecture read returned Garnet with 20 qubits.
events.explain: This proves the saved access token works — the same check that preceded T0. No credits are spent on a read.

events.title: Circuit built and compiled
events.detail: One Hadamard on each of Garnet's 20 qubits, then measure all 20. Depth 1, no two-qubit gates. Compiled to native gates only.
events.explain: The circuit is deliberately trivial: ideally each shot returns 20 independent fair coin flips. Any correlation the analyzer finds is the hardware talking, not the algorithm.

events.title: Job submitted to Garnet
events.explain: The frozen circuit is now on a real 20-qubit superconducting machine in Espoo, Finland. The job ID is the receipt anchor — everything after this is checked against it.

events.title: Counts returned from the machine
events.detail: 8192 shots returned, 8164 distinct 20-bit outcomes. Job status: JobStatus.DONE.
events.explain: Each count is a 20-bit string: one simultaneous draw from all 20 qubits. From these strings alone the analyzer computes every lane's bias and all 190 pairwise correlations.

events.title: Run record sealed
events.detail: Raw counts saved to g1-iqm-garnet-01a1664c-1d2f-7584-9acb-7204d1a29b21.json — all of them, nothing discarded.
events.explain: The counts are the evidence. Anyone with the analyzer can re-grade this run and must land on the same verdict.

events.title: Analyzer verdict: KILL
events.detail: Worst lane (qubit 12) min-entropy 0.777 bits, below the 0.85 KILL line; lane bias up to 0.0836. Only 1 of 190 lane pairs crossed the correlation line, and Hamming-weight variance was 4.997 against an ideal 5.0.
events.explain: The lanes fail on bias, not on talking to each other: qubit 12 answers 0 far too often to be a fair coin. Under the bands locked before the run, that is a KILL — Garnet's raw parallel lanes must never seed separate security receipts. The design consequence is single-lane sequential draws through a randomness extractor.
